cold_email.subject: Interest in Seasonal Full Time Educator / Hill Center Brentwood — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Seasonal Full Time Educator / Hill Center Brentwood opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Engineering Coordinator-Facilities Operations & Maintenance — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear The University of Texas at San Antonio Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Engineering Coordinator-Facilities Operations & Maintenance opportunity with The University of Texas at San Antonio at The University of Texas at San Antonio.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Temporary Research Assistant — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Rutgers University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Temporary Research Assistant opportunity with Rutgers University at Rutgers University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate Child Development Teacher - Infants and Toddlers — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Providence Health & Services Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Child Development Teacher - Infants and Toddlers opportunity with Providence Health & Services at Providence Health & Services.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Special Events Attendant opportunity with Metropolis Technologies at Metropolis Technologies.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Middle East Security Program Researcher — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Institute for the Study of War Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Middle East Security Program Researcher opportunity with Institute for the Study of War at Institute for the Study of War.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Software Developer I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear General Atomics Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Software Developer I opportunity with General Atomics at General Atomics.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Optical Lab Technician FT Waterloo, IA #079 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Eyemart Express Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Optical Lab Technician FT Waterloo, IA #079 opportunity with Eyemart Express at Eyemart Express.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Representative opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Representative — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Representative opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Program Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear VPR Patient Outreach Program Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Program Coordinator opportunity with VPR Patient Outreach Program at VPR Patient Outreach Program.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity? At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible. We are currently looking for a motivated Software Engineer with experience in writing tools and managing on-prem and help with Instrument Integration testing. Responsibilities: Applies basic problem-solving techniques to define and resolve routine issues. Determines a course of action based on guidelines. Works on assignments of limited scope where answers can be readily obtained and problem solving requires following standard practices/procedures.. Requires guided leadership and receives general instruction on work/new assignments. You will help build the team’s expanding software platform, which is the base for our applications You will consistently encounter and tackle interesting problems: Instrument Integration large data sets regulated environments portability scalability Requirements: Typically requires 0 to 2 years of previous professional experience. Programming Languages: Proficiency in at least one programming language such as Java, JavaScript, Groovy or Python. Proficiency in linux shell scripting. AI Tools: Hands on proficiency in using the AI tools like Cursor/Claude-code/VS Code or equivalent AI tools which gain productivity and increase throughput Test Automation Frameworks: Knowledge of popular test automation frameworks particularly Playwright is a must have and Rest API automation Web Technologies: Understanding of web technologies including HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. API Testing: Familiarity with API testing and understanding of RESTful APIs. Version Control Systems: Experience with version control systems like Git for managing test scripts and collaborating with other team members. CI/CD Pipelines: Knowledge of Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines and experience with Jenkins. Test Case Design: Ability to design effective and efficient test cases covering different scenarios and edge cases, as well as understanding of test data management. Familiarity with Test Management tools such as Jama/HPALM with a level of managing/creating Requirements/Specification/Test Cases/RTM and Test summary reports in the tool for tracking User Needs to Report artifacts. Problem-solving Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills to identify issues, troubleshoot failures, and debug automation scripts. Agile Methodologies: Understanding of Agile software development methodologies and experience working in Agile teams. Communication Skills: Effective communication skills to collaborate with developers, product managers, and other stakeholders. cold_email.subject: Interest in Engineer I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear General Atomics Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Engineer I opportunity with General Atomics at General Atomics.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Test & Evaluation Lab Technician (Associate or Mid-Level) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Boeing Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Test & Evaluation Lab Technician (Associate or Mid-Level) opportunity with Boeing at Boeing.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Laboratory Scientist I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Abbott Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Laboratory Scientist I opportunity with Abbott at Abbott.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Celina Lin

jobs.title: Process Engineer II
jobs.description: What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity? At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Our efforts enable life-changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients. Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible. You are the engineer Illumina is looking for. In your future role at the Madison site of the global leader in genetic sequencing, you will be part of the Engineering Services team providing process-focused engineering support for the equipment and systems producing the enzymes that fuel Illumina’s sequencing and array-based solutions. You will drive process performance through process development and design, data-driven troubleshooting, process capability assessment, yield improvement, scalable equipment solutions, process control strategy, and product and technical transfer from development through manufacturing implementation. You will support fermentation vessels, purification systems, heat treatment equipment, solids conveyance, centrifuges, chromatography instruments, cold storage, analytical equipment, and emerging platform projects. You will contribute to a self-directed, diverse team by improving process capabilities, strengthening equipment reliability, enabling scale-up readiness, and applying statistical and engineering methods to sustain control. We want your curiosity, creative problem solving, communication confidence, and drive to execute. Responsibilities Partner with cross-functional teams and vendors to support the design, troubleshooting, and improvement of manufacturing and laboratory systems, including fermentation, purification, PHT, solids conveyance, centrifugation, chromatography, cold storage, and analytical equipment. Apply process engineering principles to develop, optimize, and scale manufacturing processes and equipment using lean, Six Sigma, JMP, advanced Excel analytics, regression, DOE, statistical process control, and other data-driven methods. Use statistical analysis and engineering judgment to evaluate process performance, identify risks, improve efficiency, strengthen business continuity, and recommend maintenance, CIP, spare parts, and reliability strategies for critical manufacturing systems. Write, review, and manage engineering reports, protocols, user requirement specifications, maintenance work instructions, and technical documentation that support process design, equipment qualification, process control, and scale-up decisions. Incorporate quality, validation, and regulatory compliance requirements into system design, process engineering, equipment support, and continuous improvement activities. Develop specifications, feasibility assessments, and supporting engineering documents for scalable equipment layouts, system design, process design, qualification, and project implementation. Lead and contribute to cross-functional projects that align local, national, and international teams on process strategy, scale-up needs, equipment capability, and data-driven process improvement. Serve as a visible technical resource by mentoring supporting engineers, communicating process and system design recommendations clearly, and contributing to team culture through ownership and collaborative problem solving. Minimum Requirements: B.S. degree in Chemical Engineering or equivalent technical training/experience 2+ years relevant engineering experience. Experience in applying statistical tools, advanced Excel analytics, JMP, regression, DOE, and statistical process control to engineering reports, business cases, and process improvement decisions. Demonstrated ownership of complex, ambiguous technical work, including independent execution, high-quality documentation, and follow-through on cross-functional engineering commitments. Desire to grow toward a Senior Engineer role by leading complex cross-functional projects from concept through implementation, deepening unit operations expertise, mentoring others, and strengthening operator collaboration. The estimated base salary range for the Process Engineer II role based in the United States of America is: $76,500 - $114,700. Should the level or location of the role change during the hiring process, the applicable base pay range may be updated accordingly. The range reflects long‑term growth in the role; therefore, most candidates are hired between the minimum and middle of the range. Placement depends on experience, skills, location, and internal equity. Additionally, all employees are eligible for one of our variable cash programs (bonus or commission) and eligible roles may receive equity as part of the compensation package. We offer a wide range of benefits as innovative as our work, including access to genomics sequencing, family planning, health/dental/vision, retirement benefits, and paid time off. We are a company deeply rooted in belonging, promoting an inclusive environment where employees feel valued and empowered to contribute to our mission. Built on a strong foundation, Illumina has always prioritized openness, collaboration, and seeking alternative perspectives to propel innovation in genomics. We are proud to confirm a zero-net gap in pay, regardless of gender, ethnicity, or race. We also have several Employee Resource Groups (ERG) that deliver career development experiences, increase cultural awareness, and offer opportunities to engage in social responsibility. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer committed to providing employment opportunity regardless of sex, race, creed, color, gender, religion, marital status, domestic partner status, age, national origin or ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, pregnancy, military or veteran status, citizenship status, and genetic information. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal laws. Background check results may potentially result in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment. The background check process and any decisions made as a result shall be made in accordance with all applicable local, state, and federal laws. Illumina prohibits the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in the application and interview process. If you require accommodation to complete the application or interview process, please contact accommodations@illumina.com. To learn more, visit: https://www.dol.gov/ofccp/regs/compliance/posters/pdf/eeopost.pdf. cold_email.subject: Interest in Process Engineer II — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Illumina Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Process Engineer II opportunity with Illumina at Illumina.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Builder Education
jobs.description: About the team Customer Education helps enterprises develop the capabilities their workforce needs to use AI effectively, build and deploy AI solutions, and get more value from OpenAI’s products. About the role We’re looking for a hands-on technical educator who enjoys building with AI and helping others learn to do the same. You’ll create practical education for enterprise developers building with OpenAI’s APIs and working with Codex. You’ll turn real customer use cases into clear lessons, working examples and hands-on labs, building on our established portfolio of bootcamps, webinars and technical content. The goal is to help builders develop skills they can apply to their own applications and development workflows. This role combines technical development, learning design and live teaching. You’ll build and test what you teach, work directly with learners and create resources that can be reused across in-person, live virtual and self-paced learning. Working closely with the Builder Education team, you’ll independently own defined content, lab and delivery workstreams. You’ll partner with technical experts and customer-facing teams to keep learning accurate, useful and current as products evolve. In this role, you will: - Build practical technical education. Turn customer needs into clear learning objectives, lessons, demonstrations and exercises. Sequence concepts, practice, feedback and assessments so learners can build and apply new skills. - Create hands-on labs and learning environments. Build working examples and reliable, secure lab infrastructure. Use automation and platform integrations to make setup, access and delivery repeatable as programs grow. - Teach directly and improve through practice. Deliver in-person bootcamps and live virtual sessions, explain technical concepts clearly and help learners troubleshoot. Use their questions and feedback to improve the experience. - Own content from concept through launch. Work with technical experts to develop, test and publish content, code examples and labs. Maintain technical accuracy and update materials as products and customer needs change. - Make learning reusable. Adapt content across bootcamps, webinars and self-paced courses, and create resources that customers, internal teams and partners can use independently. - Run defined program workstreams. Manage scope, timelines and dependencies, coordinate contributors and support program operations. Build repeatable processes that keep content, environments and delivery ready for learners. - Use evidence to improve learning. Assess whether builders can apply what they learn, and work with program and analytics partners to understand how programs support product adoption and continued use. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have hands-on technical experience in software development, cloud infrastructure or AI workflows, and have built applications, integrated APIs, used Git or other version control and worked with coding agents. You can share examples of applications, API integrations or AI workflows you personally delivered. - Can turn complex technical topics into clear learning experiences, with purposeful practice and ways to assess whether learners can apply new skills. - Have built and maintained hands-on labs or technical learning environments for external customer or developer audiences, with attention to reliability, security and ease of use. - Are an engaging teacher and clear writer who can explain technical decisions, respond to learner questions and troubleshoot live. - Stay curious about AI, explore new capabilities firsthand and test the code and workflows you teach. You use learner feedback to improve your work. - Have independently owned a technical learning program from an ambiguous brief through launch and iteration, making practical scope decisions and contributing across content, teaching and program operations. - Have experience beyond education-only settings, working with product, engineering or customer teams. Experience in a fast-paced tech environment is preferred. Nice to have: - Experience with infrastructure automation tools such as Terraform and integrations that support technical labs. - Experience with learning platforms, LMS/SCORM, certification or assessment design, or learning analytics. - Relevant technical certifications or experience delivering technical training across live and self-paced formats. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Search
jobs.description: WHO ARE WE? Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company. We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems. We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that. We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft. We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us! Role overview: We are looking for talented individuals to help us develop state-of-the-art models for information retrieval as part of our Search team. This group is working on a range of tasks including training our embedding and reranker models. You'll have the opportunity to revolutionise people's search experience by contributing to building an intelligent, efficient and precise search system and you would have a lot of opportunity to try new things out, innovate, and productionize your ideas. Your work will specifically focus on advancing semantic search techniques to improve accuracy and efficiency, involving working with a wide range of novel technologies and collaborating with other teams to integrate your work into our search infrastructure. We're looking for someone who is passionate about search and has a strong background in information retrieval. Candidates should have experience working with a wide range of technologies and have worked collaboratively with other teams in the past. Key responsibilities: - Design, train and improve upon cutting-edge search models. - Gather high-quality retrieval datasets and optimize data pipelines for model training and evaluation. - Work closely with the model serving team to ensure that inference is fast and stable. - Collaborate with product teams to develop solutions. - Engage in research collaborations with our partner organizations and academic affiliations and publish your work in top-tier conferences and journals. - Join us at a pivotal moment, shape what we build, have a strong ownership mindset, and wear multiple hats! Qualifications: - Proficiency in Python and related ML frameworks such as PyTorch, Tensorflow, TF-Serving, JAX, and XLA/MLIR. - Familiarity with training and using various information retrieval models. - Experience leveraging Large Language Models as part of training data or evaluation pipelines. - Strong communication and problem-solving skills. Bonus points for: - Experience building training and/or evaluation datasets for practical use cases. - Proficiency in other programming languages, such as C++ or Golang. - Experience using large-scale distributed training strategies with GPUs. Working location: This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role. FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS: - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch. - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health. - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme. - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent. - Annual enrichment benefits: Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit. Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching. - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!) - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite. HOW AND WHERE WE WORK: - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon. - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events. - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city. - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly. If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs. We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider. Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for builders and former founders who want to take big swings at Ramp. You'll tackle important, open-ended problems, turn ideas into working products, and own what happens after launch. This is a backend engineering role for someone who wants to shape what we build, not just how we build it. Ramp's AI bets span products like Glass, an AI assistant for getting work done; Inspect, a platform for coding agents; and AI Spend Management, which helps businesses understand and manage their AI and token spend. These are examples of the problems that excite us: changing how people work, how software gets built, and how businesses put AI to use. You'll have the opportunity to build from 0–1 and scale from 1–100, bringing new AI products to life and turning early traction into lasting customer value. You'll work closely with product, design, and other engineers, stay close to users, and help find the next opportunities to accelerate Ramp's growth. You don't need to have started a company, but you should bring the same initiative, resourcefulness, and accountability. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Own products and backend systems from problem discovery and technical design through the first launch, adoption, and ongoing iteration - Turn ambiguous ideas into focused experiments, ship quickly, and use customer feedback and evidence to decide what to scale, change, or stop - Build the APIs, data models, integrations, and workflows that bring new AI products to life - Take promising products from 1–100 by improving reliability, performance, and the systems needed to support growing usage - Partner with product, design, and go-to-market teams to connect technical decisions to customer value, adoption, and Ramp’s growth - Make thoughtful bets, challenge assumptions, and balance speed with security, data correctness, and production quality WHAT YOU’LL NEED - A track record of building and shipping products people use, with meaningful ownership of the outcome - Strong backend engineering fundamentals and experience designing, building, and operating production services, APIs, and data models - Product judgment: you can identify the real user problem, question a proposed solution, and make clear tradeoffs with incomplete information - The initiative to create momentum without a complete specification, learn unfamiliar domains, and work beyond a narrow job description - jobs.description: Role Summary The Office of Software Assurance (OSA) Lead is the senior individual contributor who establishes and leads the Office of Software Assurance, a new shift-left software quality function inside the Agile Office, through technical expertise and influence rather than line management. The OSA embeds right-sized, risk-based assurance into a 1,000+ person Engineering organization, so that compliance evidence is produced as a natural, tool-native output of how teams build, not assembled after the fact. You will own day-to-day software quality execution across three lifecycle domains (SDLC, Computer Software Assurance, and Infrastructure Qualification). Natera’s Software Quality Assurance department keeps independent oversight, approval authority, and the front-line role in audits and inspections. Your focus is faster, simpler, and compliant delivery, and you do it in a way you can defend to an auditor. The ideal candidate is a software engineer first, someone who understands code, CI/CD, and engineering tooling, and who has worked close enough to regulated environments to apply quality and regulatory expectations without becoming a bottleneck. What You Will Do Stand up the OSA and execute its charter in phases: Launch (engineering-tool assurance), Extend (product-software assurance planning and evidence-readiness review), and Mature (largely automated, tool-native release-readiness evidence, with SQA operating by exception). Own the OSA Charter and the OSA Responsibility & Governance Matrix, and keep them current with SQA concurrence. Review annually or sooner as responsibilities phase in. Provide technical direction, coaching, and quality review for the OSA assurance resources, and contribute to their hiring and development plans in partnership with the Head of Agile Office. Coordinate, coach, and quality-check the engineers assigned the SQE capability within engineering teams. Define baselines and targets with the Sponsor and report on OSA success metrics: assurance turnaround and cycle time versus the legacy CSV path, deliverables per release versus the 8–10-per-release baseline, intake quality, SQA relief, inspection readiness, and capability milestones. Deliver right-sized assurance Oversee AL1–AL2 assurance planning and participate in AL3–AL4 assurance under the CSA SOP. This covers the path from CSA Intake through Software Assurance Plan, execution, report and closeout, and Service Catalog registration. Recommend the Assurance Level and assurance approach at CSA Intake. Select assurance activities and acceptance criteria from the Assurance Method Menu within an assigned level. Support SQA's level-confirmation walkthroughs. Drive a documented-critical-thinking culture. Teams should be able to explain their risk-based rationale to an auditor and apply the least-burdensome approach. Provide oversight, guidance, and continued standardization under the SDLC SOP and Infrastructure Qualification. Over time, provide product-software risk-classification input, assurance and verification planning, evidence-readiness review, and periodic review by Assurance Level. Govern engineering tools and change Own and execute the Engineering Tool Governance Work Instruction, from tool admission through retirement. Own and manage the Engineering Service Catalog, including registration of tools that hold regulated records. Oversee tool qualification. Provide fast-path change oversight and impact disposition on engineering tickets under the Software Change Work Instruction. Route device-software changes to SQA. Consult with Agile Office tooling administration on the assurance impact of tooling decisions. Partner with Software Quality Assurance (SQA) and the business Operate the inspection-readiness model: the OSA executes and supplies the technical narrative and tool-native evidence, while SQA approves determinations, plans, and closeouts and leads in audits and inspections. Provide compliant-SDLC coaching, process-feedback management, and training content. Source external training through bodies such as AAMI, ISPE, RAPS, and ASQ. Champion automation: embed evidence capture in the tools of record (for example, source control, ticketing, CI/CD, and test management), so evidence is cited by reference rather than assembled by hand. Our proprietary methods - originally developed at Stanford University - are designed to detect smaller tumors earlier and enable more personalized treatment strategies for patients with cancer. We sit at the intersection of molecular biology, bioinformatics, and next-generation sequencing (NGS), and we translate rigorous science into clinically meaningful solutions. Following our acquisition by Natera, we now combine the agility of a mission-driven startup with the scale and resources of a global leader in cell-free DNA testing. As part of our Boulder R&D team, you’ll work hands-on with scientists developing ultrasensitive, cell-free DNA technology designed to detect smaller tumors earlier and enable more personalized treatment for patients with cancer. You’ll run experiments across the NGS workflow, from gDNA isolation and library prep to hybrid capture and sequencing, using automated liquid handlers and instruments like the TapeStation and Qubit. Along the way, you’ll learn to troubleshoot, keep instruments running smoothly, and understand why an experiment behaves the way it does, not just how to run it. You won’t work in a silo. jobs.title: Supervisor, Payment Posting & Reconciliation Support
jobs.description: POSITION SUMMARY: The Supervisor of Payment Posting & Reconciliation Support oversees both the financial balancing and operational support functions within the payment posting department. This role directs the three-way reconciliation framework: verifying bank deposits against practice management system entries (AdvancedMD) and aligning daily/monthly posting activity with the general ledger accounting system (Oracle). Additionally, this role oversees the support functions within the posting department, including Vendor Invoice Management and Client Bill Posting teams. The Supervisor provides direct leadership, coaching, and analytical direction to Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) enforcing internal controls, driving compliance, and ensuring timely month-end closing support. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Reconciliation Operations & Controls: Direct and monitor daily balancing workflows between commercial/government bank deposits, lockbox activity, and practice management transactions (AdvancedMD). Reconcile AMD posting activity to the corporate general ledger (Oracle), identifying and resolving timing differences, unapplied cash, and balancing exceptions. Audit complex ERA (835) integrations and manual EOB posting files to ensure accurate allowances, contractual adjustments, patient responsibility, and copay/deductible allocations. Support month-end and year-end financial close by generating balancing files, reconciling clearing accounts, and delivering variance analyses to management. Posting Support Operations & Vendor Invoice Management: Oversee operational support functions within the posting department, ensuring timely turnaround times and accuracy across all support queues. Manage vendor invoices, tracking file placement, monitoring vendor productivity and quality, and resolving vendor reconciliation escalations. Oversee the Client Bill Posting team, ensuring accurate ledger allocation, timely invoicing application, and reconciliation of client-directed billing arrangements. Establish quality controls and audit mechanisms for third-party vendor deliverables and client invoice posting to maintain data integrity. Team Supervision & Development: Directly supervise, mentor, and evaluate SMEs setting performance standards and tracking production, accuracy, and resolution timeframes. Manage capacity planning, workflow assignment, and production coverage across daily deposit and posting cycles. Facilitate departmental onboarding, develop and maintain technical Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and deliver continuous education on emerging payer guidelines and system updates. Conduct regular performance evaluations, audit reviews, constructive coaching, and disciplinary actions in accordance with company policy. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Issue Resolution: Serve as the primary escalation point for reconciliation discrepancies, bank clearing errors, and complex payer recoupments/reversals. Liaise with Accounting, Billing, and Provider Credentialing to resolve systemic processing flaws and ensure cash flow integrity. Coordinate with internal and external audit teams to validate internal controls, separation of duties, and compliance standards. Compliance & Data Security: Maintain strict safeguards over Protected Health Information (PHI) and Payment Card Industry (PCI) data encountered during physical and digital reconciliation tasks. QUALIFICATIONS: Education: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, or an equivalent combination of education and directly relevant experience. Work Experience: Minimum of 3–5 years of progressively responsible healthcare revenue cycle experience, specifically within cash applications, payment posting, or financial reconciliation. Minimum of 2 years of direct supervisory or team lead experience managing operational/analytical staff. System Experience: Proven working experience with enterprise accounting software (Oracle strongly preferred). Direct experience with practice management/billing systems (AdvancedMD strongly preferred). KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Strong foundation in accounting basics, including double-entry reconciliation, clearing account monitoring, debit/credit mechanics, and cash-to-ledger balancing. Thorough operational knowledge of commercial, Medicare, Medicaid, and third-party payer reimbursement methodologies, including CARC/RARC codes, electronic remit clearinghouses, and recoupment workflows. Advanced analytical and spreadsheet skills (Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets), including advanced lookup functions, nested logic formulas, pivot tables, and multi-file data modeling. Demonstrated ability to synthesize financial data, diagnose root causes of variances, and prepare executive-level balance summaries. Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to manage workplace conflicts and communicate cross-departmentally with accounting and operational teams. jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role Anthropic’s Global Safety, Intelligence, and Security (GSIS) team is responsible for protecting our people, facilities, and operations worldwide. The function spans intelligence, executive protection, investigations, travel and event security, security operations, environmental health and safety, and crisis management. We are seeking a Protective Intelligence Analyst to join our GSIS team. In this role, you will play a critical part in identifying, assessing, and mitigating threats to Anthropic's people, facilities, operations, and reputation through intelligence collection, analysis, and dissemination. You'll have the opportunity to help shape the program from the ground up, establishing workflows, analytical standards, and stakeholder relationships that will scale as Anthropic grows. This role sits at the intersection of intelligence analysis, behavioral threat assessment, and executive protection. You'll produce actionable intelligence that informs security decisions across the organization and operate across the full intelligence cycle, from collection and processing to analysis, production, and dissemination, in a high-tempo environment where the threat landscape is rapidly evolving. This is an ideal role for someone who thrives on the analytical challenge of connecting disparate data points into a coherent threat picture and translating that picture into clear, actionable guidance for decision-makers. Important Note: In this position, you may be exposed to graphic and explicit content, including material of a sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing nature. Responsibilities Conduct all-source intelligence collection and analysis to identify, assess and prioritize physical security threats to Anthropic and its personnel Produce clear, well-sourced analytical products, from quick-turn updates to in-depth analytical reports for executive delivery Investigate and triage concerning communications, online threats, and persons of concern using established threat assessment methodologies Apply behavioral threat assessment principles to persons-of-concern cases, analyzing patterns of concerning behavior, indicators of escalation toward violence, and mitigating factors to guide case disposition and ongoing threat management Provide intelligence support for executive protection, travel security, and major events, including pre-travel and event briefs, assessments, and real-time threat monitoring Monitor open-source intelligence channels, social media, deep and dark web forums, and web-based intelligence platforms for emerging threats and risks Track geopolitical developments and sector-specific threat trends relevant to Anthropic’s global operations and the AI industry Build relationships with external intelligence partners, law enforcement agencies, and industry peers working on related issues and to facilitate information sharing You may be a good fit if you: Have 8+ years of professional experience in protective intelligence, corporate investigations, threat assessment, or a related discipline Hold a bachelor's degree or higher in a relevant field Have expertise in Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) tradecraft, including proficiency with specialized intelligence tools and social media analysis platforms Understand how targeted violence develops behaviorally and can recognize and weigh warning behaviors, escalation dynamics, and protective factors when assessing whether a subject is on a pathway toward harm Have hands-on experience applying established threat assessment methodologies (e.g., TRAP-18, WAVR-21) to analyze and evaluate individuals of concern Excellent communication skills, with the ability to effectively tailor complex content for various stakeholders, from technical teams to senior leadership Can manage multiple tasks simultaneously under tight deadlines with minimal oversight Have a strong drive for continuous process improvement and thrive in highly collaborative environments Are comfortable with a flexible schedule, including 24/7 on-call rotation and after-hours response, when needed Strong candidates may also have: Background in high-growth technology companies or startup Specialized knowledge of risks unique to the AI sector Professional certifications such as BTAM, CPP, PCI, or relevant intelligence community credentials Familiarity with privacy law and legal considerations governing intelligence collection in the private sector Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be received on a rolling basis. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $230,000 — $280,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Quality Engineer — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Quality Engineer opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Datacenter Server Lifecycle
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is investing $50 billion in American computing infrastructure, including datacenters custom-built for our workloads, and this role sits at the heart of that effort. As a Staff Engineer on the Datacenter Server Lifecycle team, you will own the end-to-end operational journey of every machine in our datacenters – from initial provisioning and deployment, steady-state operation, maintenance, and repair. This is greenfield work: you will help define the services, tooling, standards and processes that govern how we operate critical hardware at scale, powering frontier model development and serving. You will have the opportunity to define AI-native workflows for datacenter operations and to help drive innovations on efficiency, performance, and reliability. A distinguishing aspect of this role is its deep intersection with security. The machines in our datacenter handle some of the most sensitive workloads in AI – training frontier models and serving millions of users interacting with Claude. Ensuring that every machine in the fleet is trusted, attested, and operating with a verified chain of integrity from the hardware up is a core part of the job, not an afterthought. You will partner closely with our Infrastructure Security team to define and enforce trusted compute standards across the lifecycle, from secure provisioning through end-of-life handling. Key responsibilities Build automation to support datacenter fleets at scale. Define and own the end-to-end system lifecycle strategy – from provisioning and deployment through operation, maintenance, refresh, and decommissioning – and maintain automation and operational procedures for common lifecycle events (e.g., hardware failures, firmware upgrades, fleet rotations). Partner closely with Infrastructure Security to design and enforce trusted compute standards across the server lifecycle. Work closely with our Networking team to ensure end-to-end connectivity across all sites. Build and maintain tooling to track machine health, configuration, and operational status across the full datacenter fleet. Minimum qualifications Hands-on experience with server hardware, including rack deployment, cabling, troubleshooting, and understanding failure modes at scale. End-to-end understanding of hardware lifecycle management: asset tracking, provisioning workflows, maintenance scheduling, and decommissioning practices. Proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Python, Rust, Go, or Java). Working knowledge of modern cloud infrastructure, including Kubernetes and large scale cloud providers (e.g. AWS, Azure, GCP). Ability to communicate clearly and build consensus with a wide range of stakeholders. Comfort navigating ambiguity and making progress on complex, cross-functional problems. Willingness to travel occasionally to datacenter sites across North America. Preferred qualifications 8+ years of experience in datacenter infrastructure management, or a closely related discipline. Hands-on experience with GPU or AI accelerator hardware (e.g., NVIDIA A100/H100, Google TPUs, or AWS Trainium) and an understanding of their operational demands. Familiarity with modern provisioning and OS tooling such as LinuxBoot and NixOS Experience building or contributing to datacenter automation or fleet management platforms. Experience building and deploying server operating system distributions across large server fleets. Background in large-scale capacity planning and hardware refresh strategy, ideally at a hyperscaler or large cloud provider. Experience with trusted compute and hardware security concepts such as secure boot, TPM, hardware attestation, and firmware verification — or a strong desire to develop deep expertise in this area. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $405,000 — $485,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
